predecessors.name: Funan
predecessors.text: Chenla's base, 'Champassak in about 550', a vassal of Funan

successors.name: Land Chenla
successors.text: the northern half: 'Land Chenla is located in Isan (northeast Thailand)'

successors.name: Water Chenla
successors.text: the southern half: 'Water Chenla is situated on the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia', linked to the Mekong Delta

ledger.x: c. 550: Chenla, a vassal of Funan, rises at Champassak. 'whose base was Champassak in about 550, established their capital city at Isanapura (Sambhupura) by about 600'; infobox 'Vassal of Funan: 550' (the Funan infobox reads 'Chenla secession: 550'). The page names Champassak, not the 184,000 km2 outline; Cliopatria…

c. 598: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena attack Funan. The page dates Bhavavarman I's temple to 598 and says the two 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627-649'; the start year is bridged from the temple date (the page is silent on the first campaign), mirroring the Funan dossier.

c. 600: Chenla's capital moves to Isanapura (Sambor Prei Kuk). 'established their capital city at Isanapura (Sambhupura) by about 600'; the page also credits Isanavarman (c. 616-635) with founding it.
627: the fighting for Funan ends in Chenla's favour.
After 31 January 656 Jayavarman I conquers the principalities of north-western Cambodia.

c. 707: Chenla splits and Land Chenla forms in the north. 'shortly after 706, the country was split into Land Chenla and Water Chenla' (New Book of Tang); the Tang histories date it after 6 February 707; infobox 'Land-Water separation: c. 707'. Land Chenla 'is located in Isan (northeast Thailand)'.
c. 707: Water Chenla forms in the south. 'Water Chenla is situated on the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia' and was linked to the Mekong Delta; both halves sent tribute separately in 717.

c. 707: the undivided Chenla ends. 'Most modern historians reject a unified Chenla' (a 'series of loose and temporary confederations of principalities'; Vickery calls the Land/Water division 'misleading and meaningless'), but the Chinese sources treat the two as separate realms, so the map draws two states from 707.

wars.name: Chenla's conquest of Funan (c. 598-627)
wars.outcome: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena (Mahendravarman) 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627-649'; the Book of Sui (636) says Chenla 'annexed Funan'.

wars.name: Chenla's attempts on the Menam basin (616-657)
wars.outcome: No territorial result on the page: under Isanavarman I (616-637) 'attempts were made to extend influence into the Menam Basin, particularly toward the Tou Yuan Kingdom'; Bhavavarman II (639-657) fought 'Dvaravati Sambuka', commonly identified with Nakhon…

wars.name: Jayavarman I's conquests in north-western Cambodia (after 656)
wars.outcome: Chinese sources say he 'conquered different principalities in Northwestern Cambodia' after 656; his reign 'lasted about thirty years and ended perhaps after 690'.

certainty.note: Chenla was 'a series of loose and temporary confederations of principalities'; no page opened gives a boundary, so every frontier (the Mun valley, the Tonle Sap, the Gulf coast, the Champa border) is approximate.
